      "informal_name": "Combinatorial Nullstellensatz: Existence of Linear Combination Representation",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2} [Finite σ] [IsDomain R] (S : σ → Finset R),\n  (∀ (i : σ), (S i).Nonempty) →\n    ∀ (f : MvPolynomial σ R),\n      (∀ (x : σ → R), (∀ (i : σ), x i ∈ S i) → (MvPolynomial.eval x) f = 0) →\n        ∃ h,\n          (∀ (i : σ), ((∏ s ∈ S i, (MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C s)) * h i).totalDegree ≤ f.totalDegree) ∧\n            f =\n              (Finsupp.linearCombination (MvPolynomial σ R) fun i => ∏ r ∈ S i, (MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C r)) h",
      "informal_description": "Let $ R $ be a commutative ring with no zero divisors, $ \\sigma $ a type, and $ S_i \\subseteq R $ finite non-empty subsets for each $ i \\in \\sigma $. If a multivariate polynomial $ f \\in R[\\sigma] $ vanishes on all points $ x : \\sigma \\to R $ with $ x(i) \\in S_i $ for all $ i $, then there exist polynomials $ h_i \\in R[\\sigma] $ such that $ f $ can be expressed as a linear combination $ f = \\sum_{i} \\left( \\prod_{s \\in S_i} (X_i - s) \\cdot h_i \\right) $, where each term satisfies $ \\deg\\left( \\prod_{s \\in S_i} (X_i - s) \\cdot h_i \\right) \\leq \\deg(f) $. This representation guarantees that $ f $ is in the ideal generated by the polynomials $ \\prod_{s \\in S_i} (X_i - s) $ for each coordinate $ i $. The theorem establishes a foundational result in algebraic combinatorics, providing a certificate for polynomial identities over grids.",

      "formal_name": "MvPolynomial.combinatorial_nullstellensatz_exists_eval_nonzero",
      "informal_name": "Combinatorial Nullstellensatz: Existence of Non-Vanishing Evaluation",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2} [Finite σ] [IsDomain R] (f : MvPolynomial σ R) (t : σ →₀ ℕ),\n  MvPolynomial.coeff t f ≠ 0 →\n    f.totalDegree = Finsupp.degree t →\n      ∀ (S : σ → Finset R), (∀ (i : σ), t i < (S i).card) → ∃ s, (∀ (i : σ), s i ∈ S i) ∧ (MvPolynomial.eval s) f ≠ 0",
      "informal_description": "Let $ R $ be an integral domain, $ f $ a multivariate polynomial in $ R[\\sigma] $, and $ t $ a monomial with nonzero coefficient in $ f $ such that the total degree of $ f $ equals the degree of $ t $. For any family of finite subsets $ S_i \\subseteq R $ indexed by $ \\sigma $, if each $ S_i $ has cardinality strictly greater than the exponent of $ t $ in variable $ i $, then there exists an evaluation $ s : \\sigma \\to R $ with $ s(i) \\in S_i $ for all $ i $, such that $ f(s) \\neq 0 $. This is the combinatorial Nullstellensatz existence theorem.",

For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly.       "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {Fq : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Fq] [inst_1 : Field Fq] (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ},\n  0 < ε →\n    ∀ {b : Polynomial Fq},\n      b ≠ 0 →\n        ∀ (A : Fin n → Polynomial Fq),\n          ∃ t,\n            ∀ (i₀ i₁ : Fin n),\n              t i₀ = t i₁ ↔ ↑(Polynomial.cardPowDegree (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b)) < Polynomial.cardPowDegree b • ε",

items.informal_name: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz: Existence of Linear Combination Representation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2} [Finite σ] [IsDomain R] (S : σ → Finset R),
  (∀ (i : σ), (S i).Nonempty) →
    ∀ (f : MvPolynomial σ R),
      (∀ (x : σ → R), (∀ (i : σ), x i ∈ S i) → (MvPolynomial.eval x) f = 0) →
        ∃ h,
          (∀ (i : σ), ((∏ s ∈ S i, (MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C s)) * h i).totalDegree ≤ f.totalDegree) ∧
            f =
              (Finsupp.linearCombination (MvPolynomial σ R) fun i => ∏ r ∈ S i, (MvPolynomial.X i - MvPolynomial.C r)) h
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative ring with no zero divisors, $ \sigma $ a type, and $ S_i \subseteq R $ finite non-empty subsets for each $ i \in \sigma $. If a multivariate polynomial $ f \in R[\sigma] $ vanishes on all points $ x : \sigma \to R $ with $ x(i) \in S_i $ for all $ i $, then there exist polynomials $ h_i \in R[\sigma] $ such that $ f $ can be expressed as a linear combination $ f = \sum_{i} \left( \prod_{s \in S_i} (X_i - s) \cdot h_i \right) $, where each term satisfies $ \deg\left( \prod_{s \in S_i} (X_i - s) \cdot h_i \right) \leq \deg(f) $. This representation guarantees that $ f $ is in the ideal generated by the polynomials $ \prod_{s \in S_i} (X_i - s) $ for each coordinate $ i $. The theorem establishes a foundational result in algebraic combinatorics, providing a certificate for polynomial identities over grids.

items.informal_name: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz: Existence of Non-Vanishing Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {σ : Type u_2} [Finite σ] [IsDomain R] (f : MvPolynomial σ R) (t : σ →₀ ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.coeff t f ≠ 0 →
    f.totalDegree = Finsupp.degree t →
      ∀ (S : σ → Finset R), (∀ (i : σ), t i < (S i).card) → ∃ s, (∀ (i : σ), s i ∈ S i) ∧ (MvPolynomial.eval s) f ≠ 0
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be an integral domain, $ f $ a multivariate polynomial in $ R[\sigma] $, and $ t $ a monomial with nonzero coefficient in $ f $ such that the total degree of $ f $ equals the degree of $ t $. For any family of finite subsets $ S_i \subseteq R $ indexed by $ \sigma $, if each $ S_i $ has cardinality strictly greater than the exponent of $ t $ in variable $ i $, then there exists an evaluation $ s : \sigma \to R $ with $ s(i) \in S_i $ for all $ i $, such that $ f(s) \neq 0 $. This is the combinatorial Nullstellensatz existence theorem.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\mathbb{N} \oplus \mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: Existence of Polynomial Partition with Degree Condition
items.type:
∀ {Fq : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Fq] [inst_1 : Field Fq] (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∀ {b : Polynomial Fq},
      b ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (A : Fin n → Polynomial Fq),
          ∃ t,
            ∀ (i₀ i₁ : Fin n),
              t i₀ = t i₁ ↔ ↑(Polynomial.cardPowDegree (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b)) < Polynomial.cardPowDegree b • ε
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, positive real $\varepsilon$, non-zero polynomial $b \in \mathbb{F}_q[X]$, and function $A : \mathrm{Fin}(n) \to \mathbb{F}_q[X]$, there exists a function $t : \mathrm{Fin}(n) \to \mathrm{Fin}(\#\mathbb{F}_q^{\lceil -\log \varepsilon / \log \#\mathbb{F}_q \rceil})$ such that for all $i_0, i_1 \in \mathrm{Fin}(n)$, $t(i_0) = t(i_1)$ if and only if $\deg(A(i_1) \bmod b - A(i_0) \bmod b) < \deg(b) \cdot \varepsilon$.

items.informal_name: Partitioning Polynomials with Bounded Differences Modulo a Non-Zero Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {Fq : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Fq] [inst_1 : Field Fq] (n : ℕ) {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∀ {b : Polynomial Fq},
      b ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (A : Fin n → Polynomial Fq),
          ∃ t,
            ∀ (i₀ i₁ : Fin n),
              t i₀ = t i₁ → ↑(Polynomial.cardPowDegree (A i₁ % b - A i₀ % b)) < Polynomial.cardPowDegree b • ε
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, positive real number $\varepsilon$, non-zero polynomial $b \in \mathbb{F}_q[X]$, and sequence of $n$ polynomials $A_0, \ldots, A_{n-1} \in \mathbb{F}_q[X]$, there exists a partition function $t$ mapping indices $\{0, \ldots, n-1\}$ to $\left\lceil \frac{-\log \varepsilon}{\log |\mathbb{F}_q|} \right\rceil$ classes such that for any two indices $i_0, i_1$ in the same class, the difference $A_{i_1} \mod b - A_{i_0} \mod b$ has $\text{cardPowDegree}$ strictly less than $\varepsilon \cdot \text{cardPowDegree}(b)$. Here, $\text{cardPowDegree}$ denotes a degree-like measure combining field cardinality and polynomial degree, and $|\mathbb{F}_q|$ is the size of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$.
